value.summary: Hook: Copperdeep miners hear formal knocking and choral tones below sealed Concord galleries. Layers: trapped ghosts → ventilation, old bell pipes, and active trespass → someone searches for a tithe chamber associated with dragon history. Objectives: 1. Map safe access and protect workers from collapse or bad air. 2. Determine the source of knocking, soot, and choral resonance. 3. Decide what evidence and access should remain sealed, studied, or made public. Routes: mining expertise, sound triangulation, old plans, rescue ropes, ventilation smoke, controlled breach, magical sensing, or following trespass supply lines. Clues: human boot soot; pipes tuned to warning intervals; fresh food scraps; tithe niche marks; one knocking sequence is an old shift code. Failure forward: a gallery collapse closes one route but exposes a safer archive escape tunnel. Aftermath: bell metal carries a Kethrian tithe mark, unrelated to Alderwick tolls.

Hook: The party and Wayward Company are each hired to find “Perrin Vale,” one a missing childless merchant and the other a retired actor using the same stage name. Layers: rival rescue race → two unrelated disappearances crossing the same road → each missing person left voluntarily for a different urgent reason. Objectives: 1. Separate the identities, timelines, and actual risks without wasting rescue time. 2. Locate both Perrins or establish safe contact. 3. Resolve competing contracts fairly and protect private motives that cause no harm. Routes: cooperative task split, rivalry, road interviews, theatre records, merchant ledgers, tracking, public notices, or staged message. Clues: different boot sizes; same signature learned from playbill; two inns remember opposite food preferences; one seeks a sibling, one avoids a forced business marriage. Failure forward: one rescue succeeds first and the other person moves farther, but new contact and clues remain. Afterma…

entities.name: Q15 — A Funeral in Good Voice

value.summary: Hook: A Dunmarrow veterans' choir loses its conductor before a competitive memorial performance, and one song contains testimony challenging an honoured officer's history. Layers: petty contest sabotage → conductor withdrew over disputed verse → forged veteran claim protects a living family's status. Objectives: 1. Help the memorial proceed without treating grief as evidence theatre. 2. Authenticate the disputed verse and veteran claim through independent sources. 3. Choose a truthful form of public remembrance that does not punish innocent descendants. Routes: music, interviews, archive work, battlefield travel, private mediation, alternate performance, legal claim review, or allowing multiple verses. Clues: metre difference dates verse; pension records; Lysa Norn's melody cipher; officer's private letter; survivor accounts that disagree on motive but agree on event. Failure forward: the contest becomes acrimonious, but the memorial and later truth process can s…

Hook: A royal wedding could settle maritime claims, but Cook Berto vanishes, dock assemblies threaten to stop work, and private treaty clauses transfer an island without its delegates. Layers: comic wedding chaos → labour and representation dispute → advisers use ceremony to make contested clauses politically irreversible. Objectives: 1. Find Berto and keep essential hospitality functioning without forced labour. 2. Bring island and dock concerns into a process before vows make silence costly. 3. Protect the couple's agency while exposing, revising, delaying, or defeating hidden clauses. Routes: cooking, negotiation, strike kitchen help, legal review, island delegation, public toast, postponement, alternate venue, or private confrontation. Clues: Berto's ingredient orders feed strikers; side agreement uses obsolete island name; Princess Elia's annotations demand publication; advisers reroute delegate boats. entities.name: Q17 — The Compass of an Unbuilt Ship

value.summary: Hook: Tavaros returns a salt-worn compass engraved with the name of a ship scheduled to be built next year. Layers: prophecy → reused metal and future procurement fraud → the compass also reacts to one older Concord route no modern chart records. Objectives: 1. Authenticate materials, engraving sequence, wear, and ownership. 2. Determine how the future ship name entered the object and why Tavaros returned it now. 3. Follow or secure the hidden route without surrendering the compass to one claimant. Routes: craft analysis, dock records, question dragon witnesses, sea trial, future contract investigation, historical chart comparison, or controlled duplicate. Clues: engraving newer than wear; brass from a decommissioned ship; Pella's mentor's tool marks; needle deviation near a sealed Hall key; future contract secretly pre-awarded. Failure forward: a claimant seizes the compass, but copies, craft evidence, and Tavaros's route remain. Aftermath: the procurement fraud…

Hook: Missing League Chair Ansel Daro left three authentic resignation letters, each naming a different reason, successor, and place of refuge. Layers: indecisive politician → deliberate contingency against three anticipated kidnappers → a fourth actor helped Ansel escape all of them. Objectives: 1. Determine intended recipient and trigger for each letter. 2. Locate Ansel or establish voluntary safe contact. 3. Prevent factions from using contradictory letters to seize League process. Routes: handwriting and seal analysis, courier interviews, public procedural challenge, follow three false trails, decode grocery list, protect secret refuge, or stage a fourth resignation. Clues: different paper watermarks; one impossible seasonal fruit; punctuation as harbour basin numbers; dry-sock payment; Ansel's known habit of writing contingency apologies. Riddle: “I leave by three doors and remain in the room. Which resignation is mine?” The answer is the office, not Ansel:…

entities.name: Q19 — The Flowers Inside the Sealed Hall

value.summary: Hook: Fresh flowers appear weekly inside the Concord hall sealed since Year 1 AS. Layers: ghostly remembrance → hidden maintenance route and civic ritual → Council of Margins uses the same route to inspect archive seals. Objectives: 1. Observe or enter the Hall without damaging records or creating a public crush. 2. Identify the flower bearer, maintenance route, and separate later intruders. 3. Decide immediate custody and access while preserving evidence of Council activity. Routes: stakeout, architecture, old workers' families, roof access, drainage tunnel, ritual participation, legal petition, or magical sensing. Clues: two kinds of mud; flowers from Brokers' Orchard; old municipal invoices; wax flecks under archive door; bearer is an elderly cleaner preserving a private memorial, not the spy. Failure forward: public attention forces the Hall open under poor conditions, increasing political actors but also transparency. Aftermath: archive evidence connects Cel…

entities.name: Q20 — The Village That Is Not There

value.summary: Hook: The party follows saffron to a populated Namar village absent from tax rolls, maps, and royal service lists. Layers: smuggler settlement → community erased long ago for protection → current brokers exploit legal invisibility and Sable Annek collects erased names. Objectives: 1. Earn community consent and understand benefits and harms of invisibility. 2. Trace current grain, tax, service, and identity exploitation. 3. Pursue recognition, protected status, continued secrecy, or another negotiated form chosen with residents. Routes: puppet performance, canal work, legal research, broker infiltration, royal petition, mutual-aid records, secret census controlled by residents, or confronting collectors. Clues: songs list villages; dry-sock accounts; cargo weights; old purge order; black-scale tokens; families with births but no legal deaths. Failure forward: officials discover the place before protection is ready, creating an urgent defence and negotiation rather…

entities.name: Q21 — Seed for the Wrong Season

value.summary: Hook: Namar granaries contain short-lived seed while durable flood-resistant stock appears in foreign warehouses. Layers: theft by hungry farmers → substitution inside royal distribution → export network backed by officials and investors betting on next year's shortage. Objectives: 1. Test seed, storage conditions, and distribution records before planting. 2. Identify substitution points and protect whistleblowers. 3. Restore enough viable stock while choosing how to expose or disrupt the market scheme. Routes: agricultural expertise, warehouse tracking, controlled purchase, canal interception, public germination test, negotiation with Seed Mothers, or alternate stock exchange. Clues: husk colour, storage dust, three resignation-letter grocery list, export seals, missing barge time, one broker's unusually accurate weather insurance. Failure forward: part of the crop fails, creating relief and political consequences but also clear proof. Aftermath: a copper paymen…

Hook: Kethria's ancient copper tithe to the mountain doubles under a flawless royal order Queen Arshala denies signing. Layers: warehouse theft → ambitious Keeper using forged authority → foreign effort to wake Karsh and disrupt copper markets → real dragon bargain misunderstood by all sides. Objectives: 1. Trace copper from assay through storage, caravan, and mountain delivery. 2. Expose authorization fraud and the investors behind it. 3. Prevent, renegotiate, fulfil, or end the dangerous tithe process with informed Kethrian consent. Routes: account audit, mine infiltration, caravan protection, forge-mark comparison, council hearing, mountain ascent, dragon parley, decoy tithe, or exposing pact history. Clues: copied signature but wrong courtesy formula; warm canal; embercats; doubled foreign copper futures; old tithe objects include written climate records Karsh values.
